  "markdown": "## Business Model

Costco operates membership warehouses and e-commerce sites, emphasizing low prices on a limited selection of nationally-branded and private-label products. The company aims to achieve high sales volumes and rapid inventory turnover through volume purchasing, efficient distribution, and reduced handling in no-frills, self-service warehouse facilities [10-K line 00134]. This model allows Costco to operate profitably at significantly lower gross margins than most other retailers.

Costco's business model includes:
- Direct sourcing of merchandise from suppliers
- Cross-docking consolidation points (depots) for efficient distribution
- Self-service warehouse format with minimal frills
- Membership-based access to warehouses and e-commerce sites
- A focus on fast-selling models, sizes, and colors [10-K line 00141]
- Exclusive shopping hours for Executive members in the U.S.
- Use of various payment methods including co-branded cards, debit cards, cash, checks, reward certificates, and stored-value cards [10-K line 00140]

## Competitive Position

Costco competes globally with a wide range of retailers, including supermarkets, supercenters, online retailers, gasoline stations, hard discounters, department stores, and specialty stores [10-K line 00190]. In the U.S., significant competitors include Walmart, Target, Kroger, and Amazon. Other warehouse clubs like Sam’s Club and BJ’s Wholesale Club also compete directly with Costco [10-K line 00190].

Costco differentiates itself through:
- Low prices on a limited selection of products
- High-quality merchandise
- Private-label Kirkland Signature brand, which helps lower costs and earns higher margins [10-K line 00192]
- Member loyalty reinforced by the membership format [10-K line 00167]

## Growth Drivers

Costco's growth is driven by:
- Increasing net sales through comparable sales growth [MD&A line 00398]
- Opening new warehouses, which contributes to overall net sales growth [MD&A line 00405]
- Growing membership base and penetration of Executive memberships [MD&A line 00406]
- Rising shopping frequency from new and existing members and increased spending per visit (average ticket) [MD&A line 00398]
- Digitally-enabled sales, which represented 11% of total net sales in 2026 [10-K line 00153]
- Expansion into international markets where warehouse base is smaller and growth potential is higher [MD&A line 00405]

## Catalysts

Key catalysts for future performance include:
- Continued expansion of e-commerce operations, which offer members convenience and broader selection [10-K line 00153]
- Growth in digitally-enabled sales, which increased 21% in 2026 [MD&A line 00452]
- Successful execution of new warehouse openings, with plans to open up to 33 new warehouses in 2027 [MD&A line 00512]
- The company's ability to maintain high member renewal rates (92.3% in U.S. and Canada) [10-K line 00167]
- Continued development of private-label products, including Kirkland Signature [10-K line 00192]

## Recent Developments

Recent developments at Costco include:
- Opening 28 new warehouses in 2026 (including three relocations), with 25 net new warehouses [MD&A line 00415]
- Net sales growth of 10% to $297.2 billion in 2026, driven by comparable sales and new warehouse sales [MD&A line 00416]
- Membership fee revenue increased 11% to $5.9 billion, driven by new member sign-ups, fee increases, and Executive membership upgrades [MD&A line 00418]
- Net income increased 14% to $9.226 billion in 2026 [MD&A line 00422]
- The Board of Directors approved a 13% increase in the quarterly cash dividend in April 2026 [MD&A line 00423]
- Receipt of $184 million in IEEPA tariff refunds, net of investments in member value [MD&A line 00426]
- Expansion of bank credit facilities, increasing borrowing capacity to $2.118 billion at the end of 2026 [MD&A line 00524]

## Material Risks

Material risks for Costco include:
- Vigorous competition across a wide range of global, national, and regional wholesalers and retailers [10-K line 00190]
- Fluctuations in currency exchange rates affecting international operations [MD&A line 00409]
- Inflation or deflation in the cost of gasoline and associated competitive conditions [MD&A line 00398]
- Government actions related to tariffs, which can affect costs of merchandise [MD&A line 00403]
- Economic health impacts on member spending patterns [MD&A line 00398]
- Employee compensation costs, particularly healthcare and wage expenses [MD&A line 00407]
- Risks related to cybersecurity and privacy of member or business information [Release line 00024]
- Uncertainties in capital spending and real estate acquisition/development [Release line 00024]
- Potential impacts from geopolitical conditions, including tariffs and global conflicts [Release line 00024]

## Business Quality

Costco demonstrates high business quality through:
- Long-standing track record of profitability despite low margins [10-K line 00134]
- Strong member retention with renewal rates of 92.3% in U.S. and Canada [10-K line 00167]
- High employee retention rates (approximately 94% for employees with over one year tenure) [10-K line 00181]
- Competitive compensation and benefits that support productivity and low turnover [10-K line 00181]
- Diversified membership base with 150,400 total cardholders in 2026 [10-K line 00163]

## Competitive Advantage

Costco's competitive advantages include:
- Membership format that reinforces loyalty and provides steady fee revenue [MD&A line 00406]
- Private-label Kirkland Signature brand that enhances margins and differentiates offerings [10-K line 00192]
- Efficient distribution system with cross-docking consolidation points [10-K line 00135]
- Scale-based purchasing power that enables low prices [10-K line 00134]
- Operational efficiency through self-service format and minimal handling [10-K line 00134]

## Cyclical Exposure

Costco exhibits moderate cyclical exposure:
- Seasonal impact from winter holiday season, which drives increased net sales and earnings [10-K line 00132]
- Sensitivity to inflation or deflation in cost of goods and gasoline prices [MD&A line 00398]
- Impact of economic conditions on member spending patterns [MD&A line 00398]
- Influence of currency fluctuations in international operations [MD&A line 00409]
- Dependency on continued growth in warehouse base for net sales, though this component becomes less substantial as the warehouse base grows [MD&A line 00405]",

  "markdown": "## Thesis
Costco demonstrates a strong investment case driven by consistent growth, operational efficiency, and financial strength. The company's business model, centered on low prices, high member retention, and efficient operations, has enabled robust revenue growth of 10.1% in 2026 and strong net income growth of 14%. Key drivers include new warehouse openings, membership fee revenue increases, and digital sales expansion. Financially, Costco shows solid performance with a return on average equity of 28.4%, healthy free cash flow generation of $9.382 billion, and manageable debt levels (debt-to-equity of 0.17). The company's competitive advantages, including its private-label Kirkland brand and strong member loyalty, reinforce its sustainable position in the market.

## Recommendation
**Buy**

## Deciding Number
The **return on average equity (ROE)** of 28.4% is the key metric driving this recommendation, reflecting exceptional profitability relative to shareholders' equity and underscoring the company's efficient use of capital.",
  "recommendation": "Buy"
}

revisions.Overview:
## Overview

Costco operates membership warehouses and e-commerce sites, emphasizing low prices on a limited selection of nationally-branded and private-label products. The company aims to achieve high sales volumes and rapid inventory turnover through volume purchasing, efficient distribution, and reduced handling in no-frills, self-service warehouse facilities [10-K line 00134]. This model allows Costco to operate profitably at significantly lower gross margins than most other retailers.

Key financial highlights for 2026 include net sales of $297.2 billion, an increase of 10% year-over-year; net income of $9.226 billion, up 14%; and membership fee revenue of $5.9 billion, rising 11% due to new member sign-ups, fee increases, and Executive membership upgrades [MD&A line 00416, MD&A line 00418, MD&A line 00422].

## Market Positioning and Growth Outlook

Costco differentiates itself through a combination of low prices on a limited selection of products, high-quality merchandise, and its private-label Kirkland Signature brand which helps lower costs and earn higher margins [10-K line 00192]. The membership format reinforces loyalty and provides steady fee revenue [MD&A line 00406].

Growth drivers for Costco include comparable sales growth, opening new warehouses, expanding membership base, rising shopping frequency from members, increased spending per visit (average ticket), digitally-enabled sales which represented 11% of total net sales in 2026 [10-K line 00153], and international expansion where warehouse presence is smaller and growth potential is higher [MD&A line 00405].

Looking ahead, Costco's future outlook is supported by continued expansion into e-commerce operations offering convenience and broader selection [10-K line 00153], growth in digitally-enabled sales that increased 21% in 2026 [MD&A line 00452], and successful execution of new warehouse openings, with plans to open up to 33 new warehouses in 2027 [MD&A line 00512].

## Future Developments and Strategic Recommendations

Planned strategic initiatives include expanding e-commerce capabilities to enhance member convenience and product variety [10-K line 00153], continuing the rollout of new warehouse locations, with an emphasis on optimizing store formats for regional needs [MD&A line 00512].

Key catalysts for future performance include maintaining high member renewal rates (92.3% in U.S. and Canada) [10-K line 00167], ongoing development of private-label products including Kirkland Signature [10-K line 00192], and execution of new warehouse openings [MD&A line 00512].

Additionally, Costco is expected to continue focusing on operational efficiency through its self-service format and minimal handling, leveraging scale-based purchasing power for low prices [10-K line 00134], and expanding the membership base to drive sustainable growth across both domestic and international markets.
